seo.title: Cassandra and ScyllaDB client for {devices}
seo.description: Run CQL on Cassandra, ScyllaDB and Amazon Keyspaces over TLS, mutual TLS or SigV4. Browse keyspaces, page through tables and edit rows by primary key.

header.title: Cassandra and ScyllaDB client
header.lead: Browse keyspaces, run CQL and edit rows by their primary keys on Cassandra, ScyllaDB or Amazon Keyspaces.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter a contact point, port and any credentials, then choose a keyspace, or import a cassandra:// or cql:// URL with one in its path; open tabs keep their keyspace when you switch. TLS is off on a new connection. Preferred and Required encrypt without checking the certificate, because the driver has no opportunistic TLS; Verify CA and Verify Identity need a CA certificate file and never fall back to the system roots. For mutual TLS, add a client certificate, its key and the key’s passphrase.

Amazon Keyspaces signs in with SigV4 instead of a password. Point the connection at the regional endpoint, such as cassandra.us-east-1.amazonaws.com on port 9142, choose an AWS IAM mode, leave the user name and password empty and turn TLS on.

bands.title: Browse and run CQL
text: The grid shows collections, user-defined types, durations, vectors and blobs; editor results are read-only, so edit rows in the table opened from the sidebar. CQL has no OFFSET, so pages are read forward from the first row and a jump to a distant page reads every page before it. Rows arrive in token order, and a column header does not re-sort them. Count Exactly runs SELECT COUNT(*), which reads every partition.

Filters add ALLOW FILTERING, so the server reads every partition unless the filter pins the whole partition key. Contains, starts with and ends with need a SASI or SAI index, and conditions join with AND only, because CQL has no OR. Edits are checked as CQL types and written by the full primary key, Add Row uses INSERT … IF NOT EXISTS, and a key changes by deleting and reinserting the row. Counter columns need UPDATE … SET c = c + 1 in the editor.

bands.title: Keyspaces and tables
text: The Structure tab lists each column’s CQL type, marks partition and clustering columns as primary key, shows secondary indexes, and adds and drops columns; any other change is a CQL statement. The DDL tab rebuilds CREATE TABLE from the columns, without compaction or clustering order, so read the full definition with DESCRIBE TABLE in cqlsh.

family.title: ScyllaDB
text: ScyllaDB has its own connection type and uses the Cassandra driver over the same CQL native protocol, so connecting, browsing, editing and Cassandra’s limits apply as written. A scylladb:// or scylla:// URL creates a ScyllaDB connection.

One difference shows in the filter bar: ScyllaDB accepts contains, starts with and ends with on any column, where Cassandra needs a SASI or SAI index. Set it up as the <cassandraGuide>Cassandra setup guide</cassandraGuide> describes.

faq.question: Does TablePro show node or ring status?
faq.answer: No. There is no Server Dashboard for Cassandra or ScyllaDB. Check nodes with nodetool status, and use TablePro for keyspaces, tables and CQL.

faq.question: How do I see materialized views and user-defined types?
faq.answer: Query the system_schema keyspace in the CQL editor, for example SELECT * FROM system_schema.views or system_schema.types.

faq.question: Does TablePro connect to Cassandra 2.x?
faq.answer: No. The driver reads the schema from system_schema, which Cassandra 2.x does not have, so the connection fails.
